title: Senegalese dishes her grandmother cooked
summary: Pepe-pate, red beans with bananas, tum tum and gumbo; Zeno misses her grandmother.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: And what did she call the puddings? What did she call the pudding that you made?
Well, that's French. Yes, pepe-pate is French.
That was that sweet potato pudding.
Made great. Not boiled, no. Grate. You grate it? And you put plenty of black pepper in it.
Oh, really hot then, is it?
I didn't like it much on account of that pepe-pate, that black pepper, you know? Yes. And she used to make funny dishes, you know, her home dish.
What other kind of dishes did they have?
Oh, red beans and bananas. That sounds good to me. I like both of them.

I like it. I like all the galamacha, as my mom called it. All what my grandmother cooked. It was fine. Where did red beans and bananas come from? From Senegal. That's a Senegal dish. And what are some of the other Senegal dishes? Well, they had tum tum. And that is? Tum tum is okra cooked with sweet potato, but the white sweet potato. That's tum tum.
And did they make gumbo in Senegal, or do you know? Yes, they made gumbo. What kind of gumbo would they make? Well, okra.
They make tum tum. Both okra and gumbo are African words. Did you know that?

Well, my grandmother used to cook it. And she'd fried bananas with ham. I miss my grandmother. I wish she was over a hundred when she died, so I know she'd be just like a monkey now. But I miss her. I miss her.
